name: Splash / Home
engineEndpoint: none/static for the shell; RECENT list would read prior solves (app/api/usage/route.ts or app/history) — no telemetry/personalization copy allowed
dataSource: Static React shell + (optional) recent-solves read; no engine call on load
buildNotes: A home screen exists but the layout diverges from the mockup. Mockup is input-first: centered GONR wordmark, the two-line promise 'Know what to do. / Know what not to.', then a single prominent free-text field 'What's going on?' with a pink 'Ask GONR' pill button as the primary CTA into the flow. Below it a 'RECENT' section with a 'View all' link and a vertical list of past items (thumbnail + 'Red wine on white cotton shirt' + relative time). Bottom tab bar: Home / History / Saved / Profile (mockup uses 4 tabs, not the current Home/History/Care/Pro-Help + center scan FAB). Reskin HomeScreen.tsx to: (a) lead with the free-text question box, not the 'Scan a stain' card; (b) replace the 3-up Scan/Care/Upload grid with a single text entry that opens the Attach Menu (screen 2) via a '+' / attach affordance; (c) render RECENT as a real list bound to history data, with an empty-state when none. Keep GONR-only gradient wordmark, pink/magenta/orange/navy palette, GREEN-FREE.
safetyNotes: Home is pure entry — render NO verdict, treatment, or 'safe to try' language here. Do not imply the camera/photo alone yields certainty ('Scan a stain' must read as starting context intake, not an answer). Keep honest framing: no fabricated counts, no 'personalized for you' claims on RECENT, no social-proof telemetry. The promise line 'Know what NOT to do' is the brand's safety-first hook — preserve it; it sets the expectation that GONR will sometimes say stop.

'Scan Care Label' is the key safety affordance: it teaches users that fiber + care symbols drive what is safe, so surface it prominently (do not bury it under the stain-photo options). Do NOT promise the photo identifies the stain with certainty — vision confidence can be 'low' and must be treated as a hint that the Chat screen will confirm, never an authoritative verdict. Care-label warnings (e.g. dry-clean-only, do-not-bleach) must flow downstream and never be overridden by a stain-photo guess. Product Label and Voice Note rows must degrade gracefully (no dead taps) since their endpoints are not yet built.

engineEndpoint: app/api/solve/route.ts (returns disambiguation_prompt for ambiguous input) + data/predictive-intake-gate-spec.json (drives which clarifying questions to ask / forces full intake on high-risk-unknown flags); pre-fill from app/api/scan-stain + app/api/scan-label
dataSource: Clarifying-question set from predictive-intake-gate-spec.json + solve route disambiguation_prompt; user answers populate the SolveInput context object
buildNotes: Build a chat-style intake screen: top shows the captured-context chip (thumbnail + 'Red wine on white cotton shirt'), then a GONR assistant bubble that (a) reflects back what was detected and (b) asks 2-3 short clarifying questions as a bulleted list (mockup examples: has the garment been washed/dried? is the stain wet or dry? what type/age?). The SPECIFIC questions must come from the engine/intake-gate, not be hard-coded chemistry — render whatever the gate/disambiguation_prompt returns. Bottom is an 'Ask a follow-up...' text input. As the user answers, accumulate facts into the SolveInput object (material, stainType, care, heat, colorfastness, age, value, priorTreatments) that ConsumerSolveShell already models, then advance to the Details Collected summary (screen 4). Reuse ConsumerSolveShell's option vocabularies as the answer-mapping target; replace its form chrome with conversational bubbles + quick-reply chips.
safetyNotes: This is the safety-gate screen — the questions exist to AVOID giving advice on missing facts. Per predictive-intake-gate-spec.json GLOBAL-001, any high-risk-unknown flag (delicate/specialty fiber, leather/suede/aniline, unknown dye stability, unknown stain identity, prior home treatment, heat exposure, luxury/trimmed garment) must FORCE full intake — do not let users skip questions into a confident answer. Keep the 'act fast on fresh stains' framing as general urgency only; do NOT emit any treatment step or chemical here — that is screen 5 behind the engine. Reflect detected facts honestly (mark vision-detected fiber/stain as 'looks like', confirmable). Never invent a stain identity the user did not confirm; 'unknown' is a valid, safe answer that downgrades, not escalates, certainty.

buildNotes: Build a read-back summary screen: same context chip at top (thumbnail + 'Red wine on white cotton shirt'), a 'Your details' card listing the collected facts as short rows (mockup: 'Not washed', 'Stain wet', 'Red wine (unknown type)') — each row is one confirmed SolveInput field, rendered from state, not hard-coded. Below: a 'Got it. Here's the best approach for this situation.' transition line, then a 'Sources' footer crediting 'GONR Encyclopedia + LLM Analysis'. The 'Sources' values must reflect the actual solve response source (verified card vs AI fallback) — do not always show both. Tapping through POSTs the assembled context to /api/solve and advances to Results. Keep the 'Ask a follow-up...' input present so users can correct a fact (which should re-open/patch the intake, not silently ignore). Per the response-must-match-DB-state rule: render the details exactly as collected, never defaults.
safetyNotes: This screen is the consent/transparency checkpoint before any guidance — it must let the user catch a wrong fact (e.g. fiber misidentified, 'unknown' where they actually know) before the engine answers, because every downstream step keys off these facts. The Sources line is a trust/honesty surface: if the answer is AI-fallback, the source must say so (carry ai_fallback_disclosure), never overstate 'Encyclopedia-verified'. Do not preview any treatment step or 'safe' verdict here — only echo facts and route to the engine. If solve returns noVerifiedProtocol or a stop/do-not-attempt verdict, this screen must not have implied a fix was coming.

name: Results / Solution (step-by-step)
engineEndpoint: app/api/solve/route.ts (POST) — renders card.title + card.spottingProtocol[] {step, instruction}; OR the local deterministic path lib/consumer-safety/classifier.ts -> SafetyVerdict.card -> CONSUMER_CARDS_PHASE0.safeSteps[]. ConsumerSolveShell currently uses the local classify() path.
dataSource: card.spottingProtocol (AI/library protocol from /api/solve) or renderedCard.safeSteps (lib/consumer-cards/cards.ts) for the numbered steps; card.title for the heading; card.materialWarnings / verdict.reasons for the 'Important notes' accordion.
buildNotes: Build a dedicated, mockup-faithful ResultsScreen component (the screens/ dir only has HomeScreen.tsx today; the logic lives inline in ConsumerSolveShell). Match the mockup: header 'Recommended for you', a white card holding a vertical numbered list where each step is a numbered pill + a bold short action title + a one-line body (e.g. '1 Blot (don't rub)' / supporting sentence). The mockup shows ~4 steps; render exactly what the engine returns (cap display per the engine's 5-8 step contract) — do NOT hardcode a step count. Below the steps, a collapsible 'Important notes' accordion (pink-tinted, chevron) that expands to material warnings. Brand: pink/magenta/orange/navy, GREEN-FREE (the current ConsumerSolveShell uses green #1F7A52 swatches — that violates the TASK-218 green-free lock and must be re-skinned for the consumer surface). Keep the 'Ask a follow-up' footer input as a stub. Map each engine field to a slot; never author step text in the component.
safetyNotes: Safety-first ordering is the whole point of this screen: the FIRST step the engine returns is the safe-first move (blot/cold-water/test-first) and must render at position 1, never buried. Do NOT invent or reorder steps — order comes from card.spottingProtocol exactly as the engine emits it. Surface card.materialWarnings prominently (the 'Important notes' accordion must be visible/affordant, not hidden so far it's missed) because that is where fiber-risk teaching lives ('teach them enough not to ruin the garment'). Honor sanitizeCardForTier: the consumer/home view must never show products.professional or pro spottingProtocol leaked from the engine. If source='ai-unavailable' or ai_fallback_disclosure is present, render that disclosure banner verbatim so the user knows steps are general, not stain-specific.

name: Do-Not-Do (what makes it worse)
engineEndpoint: app/api/solve/route.ts -> card.materialWarnings[] (fiber/material 'do not' guidance injected by injectContextWarnings/applyFiberModifications) plus the safety filter; AND lib/consumer-safety/classifier.ts -> SafetyVerdict.avoid[] (the 'Avoid' array currently rendered inline in ConsumerSolveShell).
dataSource: verdict.avoid[] (consumer-safety classifier) and/or card.materialWarnings[] (/api/solve). Each array entry is one 'do not X' line authored upstream by the engine/safety layer.
buildNotes: Build a standalone Do-Not-Do panel/screen matching the mockup: header 'Things to avoid (for this stain)', then a vertical list of rows, each a red X icon (lucide XCircle) + a short bold prohibition line + optional one-line reason ('Do not use heat until the stain is gone', 'Do not put in the dryer — heat can set the stain', 'Do not use chlorine bleach on colored fabrics', 'Do not rub the stain — this can spread it'). Use red/pink severity styling per the 'ship CSS with severity classes' rule — this screen conveys danger and must read as warnings, not neutral bullets. Iterate over the engine's avoid/warnings arrays; render exactly what's returned, do not cap to a fixed 4. Keep 'Ask a follow-up' footer stub. This can be its own screen OR a strongly-styled section co-located with Results (screen 5) — but it must be visually distinct from the allowed steps so the two are never confused.
safetyNotes: This is the highest-stakes teaching surface and the reason the tool earns trust: wrong-move avoidance prevents the user from permanently ruining the garment (heat-setting protein, bleach on color/wool/silk, rubbing/spreading, dryer before the stain is gone). EVERY line must come from the engine's avoid/materialWarnings output — do NOT invent prohibitions or chemistry in the component; the deterministic safety filter and fiber-modification logic are the source of truth. Do not soften, summarize, or drop any returned warning to fit the layout (note the existing inline render does .slice(0,5) on avoid — a dedicated Do-Not-Do screen should show ALL returned items, not truncate safety content). Pair the prohibition with its reason when the engine provides one so the user learns the 'why', not just the 'don't'.

name: Care Label Info (fabric + care symbol decode)
engineEndpoint: app/api/scan-label/route.ts (POST) -> lib/vision/index.ts readCareLabel() -> { fiber: string, careSymbols: string[], warnings: string[], confidence }. careSymbols are string tokens e.g. 'dry-clean-only','no-bleach','no-heat','hand-wash-only','do-not-wash','no-iron','machine-wash-warm','tumble-dry-low'.
dataSource: /api/scan-label response: fiber -> 'Fabric' value (e.g. '100% Cotton'); careSymbols[] -> the decoded 'Care' rows; warnings[] -> caution lines. The fabric-durability summary ('Good news! Cotton is durable...') should be driven by engine/encyclopedia material context, not hand-authored per fabric.
buildNotes: CareLabelScanner.tsx exists but only does the capture->fetch->callback handoff (it passes fiber+careSymbols to the parent); there is NO render UI matching the mockup and NO care-symbol decode table in the repo. Build a CareLabelInfo screen: header 'Care label analysis', a 'Fabric' card showing the fiber string, then a 'Care' card listing each care symbol as a row = symbol glyph/icon + plain-language label (e.g. 'Machine wash warm', 'Do not bleach', 'Tumble dry low', 'Do not iron', 'Dry clean'). This requires a NEW display-layer decode map (token -> {icon, human label}) covering the lib/vision token vocabulary — this is presentation/copy, not stain chemistry, so it is in-scope to author. Source care-symbol glyphs from a licensable/standard ASTM/ISO-style set or simple lucide approximations; do not pixel-trace. Add the plain-language fabric summary block at the bottom fed by engine material context. Keep confidence handling: if confidence='low' or fiber empty, show a 'couldn't read the label clearly' state, not a fabricated fabric.
safetyNotes: The care label is the user's single most reliable fiber/material signal, which gates everything downstream (no-bleach, hand-wash-only, dry-clean-only all change what is safe). Decode honestly: never upgrade or guess a symbol that wasn't detected — render only careSymbols the engine returned, and surface readCareLabel warnings[] verbatim. Frame this screen as teaching the user to read their own label so they don't ruin the garment (e.g. a 'do not bleach' symbol means skip every bleach/peroxide step). Do NOT author fabric-specific cleaning advice or chemistry here ('Cotton is durable and can handle most stain removal methods' style copy must come from the encyclopedia/engine material context, not be invented in the component). When fiber feeds the solve flow, the no-bleach / hand-wash / dry-clean flags must propagate as constraints (applyFiberModifications already does this on /api/solve) — this screen should make that linkage visible, not just decorative.

name: Follow-up / Clarify
existingPath: /Users/tyler/dev/gonr-app-task218-lab/components/consumer/ConsumerSolveShell.tsx (has the 'Ask a follow-up…' input surface); disambiguation backend in /Users/tyler/dev/gonr-app-task218-lab/lib/protocols/ambiguity.ts
engineEndpoint: /Users/tyler/dev/gonr-app-task218-lab/app/api/solve/route.ts — re-call with refined query; returns either a normal solve card OR a `disambiguation_prompt` object {question, options[]} (from getDisambiguationPrompt) plus `original_query`
dataSource: Two engine shapes feed this screen: (1) a clarifying question the engine asks back — `disambiguation_prompt.question` + `disambiguation_prompt.options[]` (lib/protocols/ambiguity.ts decision trees, e.g. 'What kind of mark is this?'); (2) a user free-text follow-up ('What if it's an old stain?') that re-hits /api/solve with the refined stain string (the Unknown path appends `-unknown-general` to signal explicit consent to a baseline answer). Response then carries the updated card fields (steps, whyThisWorks, notes).
buildNotes: Build the conversational follow-up turn from the mockup: the prior context shown as a small grey quoted bubble ('What if it's an old stain?'), then GONR's tailored answer rendered as a short structured block ('For old, set-in stains, try this approach:' → bulleted steps like soak in cold water + oxygen powder, use an enzyme treatment, repeat before washing → a realistic-expectations footer 'Results may vary depending on fabric and dye.'). Persistent 'Ask a follow-up…' input pinned at the bottom (already present in ConsumerSolveShell) drives a re-solve. When the engine returns a `disambiguation_prompt` instead of a card, render the question text and the option list as tappable chips/buttons; selecting one re-solves with that refined token. Keep each follow-up answer in the same scroll thread so it reads like a continued conversation, not a fresh page. Render bullets/steps from engine card fields — do not template fixed advice.
safetyNotes: This is the core teaching loop — the answer must carry the safety frame forward, not drop it: every follow-up response should preserve the original verdict level and warnings (the engine's VerdictLevel: diy_safe / diy_with_constraints / stop_use_pro / do_not_attempt) so a user can't 'ask their way around' a do-not-attempt verdict. The realistic-expectations footer ('results may vary') is safety copy, not marketing — keep it. For the Unknown/baseline path, the UI must show the engine's up-front honesty banner that this answer is general, not stain-specific. Never let a follow-up re-render advice that contradicts a prior fiber/heat warning; if the engine returns a softened card, show it, but the UI must not synthesize new chemistry to fill a gap. Do NOT invent the clarifying questions — they come from ambiguity.ts trees.
